correctness.rationale: Every periodic W^{1,infinity} derivative has mean zero and any bounded mean-zero function has a periodic Lipschitz primitive; commuting derivative with convolution reduces induced Lip seminorm to L∞–L¹ duality modulo constants. A median c of the nonconstant Fejér kernel minimizes absolute deviation; its zero-measure level sets yield an attained derivative sign(F_n-c). For odd n=2m+1, sign(F_n-1/n)=sign(sin((m+1)t)sin(mt)), which flips under t→t+pi, so c=1/n is median. Kernel F2/F3 give the exact cases. For asymptotics n F_n(t) converges weakly in distribution by joint torus Fourier-character equidistribution to H=sin²U/sin²V with independent U,V uniform, whose unique median is 1. Median convergence plus bounded truncation n(1-L_n)=2 E min(nF_n,c_n)-c_n avoids invalid unbounded dominated convergence. Integrating the two-angle triangle gives E min(H,1)=1/2+2/pi², yielding 4/pi². Fresh independent high-resolution midpoint quadrature verifies L2,L3, odd n median and n=200 limit approximation 0.405300 versus 0.405285, but unbounded n uses the rigorous proof.

value.rationale: This sharp first-order contraction coefficient answers a natural stability question for classical Fejér summability on periodic Lipschitz functions, including exact extremizers and asymptotic rate. It is not merely another approximate-identity convergence estimate or unmotivated numeric constant.

final_claim: For real periodic Lipschitz functions on T with normalized Haar measure, Fejér convolution T_n has exact seminorm contraction factor L_n=min_c∫|F_n-c|dμ with median extremizers, odd n>=3 median exactly 1/n, L2=2/pi, L3=8/(3pi), and lim_{n→∞} n(1-L_n)=4/pi².
limitations: Real-valued periodic Lipschitz functions and ordinary first-order Fejér kernels; for even n the exact median is implicit, and only the leading deficit term is proved.
